title: Route-level unit economics computation pipeline (amortized cost & latency attribution)
creator: Alma Rios
description: Implement a dedicated computation service that emits per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns with correct amortization of shared resources (batching, KV cache, GPU warmups). The goal is to provide the Console and billing pipeline with: (1) near-real-time derived metrics for dashboards and anomaly detection, and (2) day-rollup facts that reconcile to the billing ledger. This service should handle: tokenization variance, model variant family mapping (eg gpt-style vs open models), multi-tenant dedicated pools, and fallback routes. It must not duplicate billing logic but produce explainable, auditable decomposition used by cost-explorer and SLA reports.
acceptance_criteria: Per-route and per-model daily rollups are available in ClickHouse with <1% reconciliation drift vs billing ledger for last 7 days
Streaming hourly breakdowns are emitted to metrics topic with schema v1 and can be consumed by Console dashboards
Amortization rules applied for batching and KV cache produce stable attribution across synthetic load tests (see test plan)
Service exposes an explain endpoint that returns decomposition trace for a single request id (latency buckets, kernel time, batching credits, cache hits)
Backfill job can compute historical decompositions for up to 90 days within 48 hours for a 30TB event set
notes: We observed confusion in Console where per-route latency appeared lower than per-model because GPU kernel warmups and batch compaction were unaccounted for — this project will normalize accounting across layers.
Prefer stream-first architecture: Kafka -> Flink (stateful aggregation & amortization windows) -> ClickHouse for OLAP + materialized hourly topics for low-latency Console reads.
Cost model inputs: kernel_time_ms (sampled from runtime), tokens_generated, input_tokens, model_variant (quantized flag), instance_type, gpu_minutes billed, amortized_shared_batch_slots.

We will use a combination of deterministic rules (KV cache amortization = saved tokens * model_specific_rate) and sampled telemetry (kernel timing percentiles) to estimate per-token compute cost where exact billing isn't available.
This service must emit provenance metadata (version, ruleset hash) so Console can show which decomposition rules produced a number. Keep ruleset stable across rollouts and versioned in Git.
Important: final numbers used for customer invoices remain in billing-ledger; this service is for observability & internal chargeback decisions but must reconcile closely to avoid confusion.

implementation_plan: Phase 0: Spike (done) — validate telemetry signals and cheap estimators for kernel_time_ms and KV cache savings.
Phase 1: Streaming pipeline — ingest events from kafka.topics.inference.requests and runtime.telemetry; implement Flink job for per-request decomposition and windowed amortization (1m,1h,daily)
Phase 2: OLAP + materialized topics — write hourly and daily rollups to ClickHouse and publish summarized topic kafka.topics.metrics.route_econ.v1
Phase 3: Explainability API — lightweight service that joins rollup shards and runtime samples to present decomposition traces for a request id
Phase 4: Backfill tooling — Spark job for historical recompute and reconciliation report against billing ledger
Phase 5: Monitoring and dashboards — create Console widgets, anomaly alerts, and SLOs for reconciliation drift
rollout_plan: Canary: enable decomposition for 5% of traffic routed to region us-west-2 (feature flag route_econ_v1)
Validate canary against synthetic load and reconciliation target (<2% drift) for 72 hours
Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% across regions after signoff from PM and finance
Publish ruleset hash and version to Console where customers can opt into seeing more granular breakdowns
Cutover: start publishing hourly materialized topic and update Console queries to read new source (grace period: 14 days)
monitoring_checks: Flink job checkpoint interval < 90s and no checkpoint failures in last 24h
ClickHouse daily rollup job completes within 2 hours of cutover window
Reconciliation drift vs billing ledger (7-day rolling) < 1% (alert at 2%)
Explain endpoint latency p95 < 200ms for cached traces
estimated_cost_impact: We expect this to surface 8-12% reattribution of cost to routes with high micro-batching and long KV-cache hits; not expected to change billed amounts but will change Console-visible cost allocation used by teams.
decisions: Use Flink for stateful streaming aggregation due to complex amortization windows and requirement for exactly-once output
Store final rollups in ClickHouse for fast Console queries; use compacted Kafka topic as warm cache for near-real-time reads
Sampling at runtime for kernel_time_ms will be used instead of full per-token instrumentation to limit overhead; sampling rate configurable per-cluster
blockers: Need final schema approval from finance for mapping kernel_time -> billing units (waiting on PM-842)
Runtime team needs to add request_id and kernel_time_ms to telemetry events for quantized models (expected by 2026-02-28)
